newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures settle higher on firm cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures settle higher on firm cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Monday on a rise in the western U.S. cash market and a Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) price hike, market sources said.
"It's BPA prices, and just a lot of people who were short-covering October," said one Houston trader.
BPA raised most of its next-day firm offer prices during peak hours 0600-2300 PDT at $21.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from $20.00 between 0800 and 2100 on Monday.
Expectations of the last bout of air-conditioning demand in the Southwest through next week also supported cash prices.

Today's forecasts showed temperatures in southern Nevada and most of Arizona to peak in the 90's to 100's Fahrenheit degree range and to bottom in the 60's. The six to 10 days outlook showed those regions would receive warmer-than-normal weather.
November California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up 34 cents at $17.44 a MWh after being traded between $17.10 and $17.70.
December COB climbed 15 cents to $18.55. Deferred COB months finished five to 10 cents higher.
November Palo Verde (PV) futures ended up 35 cents to $16.60 a MWh, near its day's high opf $16.65.
December PV rose 30 cents to $17.35. Outer PV months closed 20 cents higher.
